solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Park, perhaps, where bird stands on a rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
in a down clue, standing up means the bird's letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the mina is a variant spelling of the mynah, an Asian starling
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A description of a park scene with a bird perched on a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park' looks like green space; it is Nick Park, maker of Wallace and Gromit. MINA turned upward gives ANIM, placed above A and TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Park is a famous British maker of clay stop-motion films, so he is an example of this profession.

clue.text: See 20
Setter managed to bite neck, a painful one 15 24 33

parts.note: the sun is a setter because it sets every evening, not the crossword compiler

indicators.note: biting means taking something between the teeth, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: managed means did, as in 'did without'

indicators.note: something painful is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword setter manages to nip someone's neck, an act of painful cowboy play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts as the compiler; it is the sun. 'painful' rearranges NECK A to ANCEK, which DID bites. 15 24 33 reads 'playing at sixes and sevens', that is playing 6 and 7 down: cowboys and Indians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sundance Kid was the Wild West outlaw partner of Butch Cassidy, so a character in any game of cowboys and Indians.

clue.text: Skin cold — then what one might apply?

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
heat is what one applies to a sore muscle, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone with chilled skin wonders what remedy they should apply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skin' reads as the body's covering but is the verb meaning to fleece someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To skin someone is slang for swindling them out of money, the same as to defraud or con.

clue.text: Lacking any vision, outrageous male appearing as drag queen?

indicators.note: a man appearing as a drag queen is someone placed inside a frock, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man, here a dress

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wild behaviour, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An outrageous man turns up in drag as a queen, which nobody foresaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag queen?' is the picture of a man in a frock: 'appearing as' puts the jumbled man ('outrageous') inside the frock, and 'queen' just completes that image.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamless sleep has no dreams in it, so it lacks any vision in the night.

clue.text: Amateurish, reluctant to be punched by body of fighters

indicators.note: being punched by something means it is driven into you, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: coy means reluctant or bashful
the WBO is the World Boxing Organization, a governing body for professional boxers

explanation.surface: A shy beginner is reluctant to face the punches of a group of boxers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy builder or plumber is an unqualified, slapdash tradesman, so the adjective means amateurish.

clue.text: National support raised through drinks supplier

indicators.note: one piece runs through the middle of the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: an inn is a pub, which supplies drinks

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upward

parts.note: aid means help or support

explanation.surface: National funding is channelled through a company that supplies drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AID upward to DIA, which goes through INN.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of India is called by this demonym, so it is a nationality, a person of a particular nation.

parts.note: 24 33 means disordered, so this asks for the letters of 'or he's' scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone playing at cowboys is in fact in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 24 33 reads 'playing at sixes and sevens': 6 and 7 down, cowboys and Indians. The second 24 33 means mixed up, so the answer reads as an instruction to scramble a steed, which gives 'or he's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy Horse was a Lakota war leader at the Little Bighorn, one of the Indians in any game of cowboys and Indians.

clue.text: Two-thirds of the planet in recession including posh little nation

indicators.note: including means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
in recession means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left
two-thirds of a six-letter word keeps four letters, dropping the last two

parts.note: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun
U means upper-class or posh, as in 'U and non-U' English

explanation.surface: An economic report: a planet's economy shrinks, sparing only a rich little country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds of' trims URANUS to URAN; 'in recession' turns it to NARU, which takes in U. 'in recession' reads as economic decline but is a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny Pacific island republic, one of the smallest sovereign states in the world.

clue.text: Someone unable to speak, one runs, seeing killer at sea

parts.note: Harpo Marx of the Marx Brothers never spoke on screen
R is the cricket scoreboard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A mute person flees after witnessing a murderer on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon-thrower on a whaling ship kills whales, so is a killer at sea.

clue.text: Such histrionics died in recollection of part secured by papa's partner

indicators.note: being secured by something means being held fast within it

parts.note: mama goes with papa as the pair of parents

indicators.note: one piece sits in another
re-collection, gathering back, signals that the word is read backwards

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An actor's overacting over a death scene, the part secured through Mum's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollection of' (re-collection, a gathering back) is the reversal signal, though it reads as memory; 'papa's partner' is the other parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodrama is exaggerated, sensational emotion, the very stuff of overacted histrionics.

clue.text: Unknown character behind individual in snack attack

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this piece follows the rest
one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
I, the Roman numeral one, is a single individual
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns; z is a letter, a character

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure attacks someone's snack from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitz is a sudden intense assault, from the German Blitzkrieg, lightning war.

clue.text: No-nonsense tarot card's acceptance

indicators.note: no in front of a word means without it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: rot means nonsense, as in 'talking rot'
the king is a court card in a pack

explanation.surface: A down-to-earth fortune teller accepts the tarot card that is drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-nonsense' reads as one adjective meaning practical, but it splits: 'No' is the deletion signal and 'nonsense' the letters taken from 'tarot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking means receiving or accepting, as in the taking of an offer.

clue.text: See 3
Phosphorous spreading on the field

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
laying, as in laying a carpet or laying down a layer, means spreading

explanation.surface: A farmer spreads phosphorus fertiliser over a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in a game is out on the field of play, actively taking part.

clue.text: Wildebeest's twisted tail — or arm

indicators.note: the tail of the word, its last two letters, is turned round

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A wildebeest's tail is twisted, or perhaps one of its limbs is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted tail' swaps the last two letters of GNU.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is a weapon, and a firearm is the commonest sort.

clue.text: One going downhill describing fluctuating rate that's less consistent

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a skier goes down the slopes

indicators.note: fluctuating means varying back and forth, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A skier whose speed varies on the way down is not very reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuating' turns RATE into TREA, which SKIER surrounds ('describing').
explanation.definitionFit: A streaky performer has runs of good and bad form, so more streaky means less consistent.

clue.text: Termed a sort of iron-rich item

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them into another order

explanation.surface: Something has been labelled a kind of iron-rich food.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef and lamb are rich in iron, and this food category is a dietary source of it.

clue.text: She's reigned for nearly 60 years, a long period

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Queen Elizabeth II, who had reigned almost sixty years when this appeared

explanation.surface: A tribute to a monarch whose long reign spans an age.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long span of history, an age or epoch.

clue.text: One 15 24 33, one charging by the session

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a sitting is a session, as of a court or parliament
a bull is an animal known for charging

explanation.surface: A cowboy-game player and someone who bills by the session.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 24 33 reads 'playing at sixes and sevens', that is playing 6 and 7 down: cowboys and Indians.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting Bull was the Hunkpapa Lakota chief at the Little Bighorn, an Indian in any game of cowboys and Indians.

clue.text: Item for the range, perhaps, range perhaps for 14, perhaps

parts.note: a tee is used at a golf driving range

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters might be arranged otherwise, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A deliberately repetitive puzzle about golf ranges and kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'range' is a golf driving range; the second is anagram fodder, with 'perhaps' after it as the signal. 14 is KID, and a kid may be in their teens.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid can be anyone young, a teen among them, so this is one example of a kid.

clue.text: Monkey cuddled by chimpanzee

indicators.note: being cuddled means being held inside someone's arms, so the letters sit within the word

explanation.surface: A young monkey is hugged by a chimp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' reads as the animal but means a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A little monkey is a mischievous child, the same as a little devil or rascal.

clue.text: One 15 44 33, he's called for the high jump?

definitions.meaning: an Apache leader, one of the Indians in a game of cowboys and Indians

definitions.text: he's called for the high jump?
definitions.meaning: the name is the cry shouted by a paratrooper leaping out of a plane

explanation.walkthrough: 44 is a slip for 24: 15 24 33 reads 'playing at sixes and sevens', that is playing 6 and 7 down, cowboys and Indians.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was the Apache war leader, and US paratroopers shout his name as they jump from aircraft.

clue.text: Sadness with it, a drunk stealing kiss, a fair chance disorderly

indicators.note: stealing something means taking it in, so one piece is held inside the other
drunk suggests something reeling about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: X is the sign for a kiss at the end of a letter
evens are fifty-fifty odds, a fair chance

explanation.surface: A sad drunk snatches a kiss, a fair chance of things getting out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges SADNESS IT A to ATSIESANDS, which 'stealing' X makes ATSIXESANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of muddle and confusion is the meaning of this idiom, so it fits disorderly.

clue.text: Flag carries promotion for lecture

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A flag is used to advertise a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' reads as a banner but is the verb meaning to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a harangue, much like a scolding lecture.

clue.text: Nice summer in Africa getting half cut — it's the cold drink

indicators.note: one piece sits in another
cutting half the word away removes three of its six letters

parts.note: été is French for summer, as spoken in Nice

explanation.surface: A pleasant African summer leaves someone tipsy, so they settle for a cold drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like 'pleasant' but is the French city, so its summer is in French; 'half cut' looks like tipsy but halves the continent's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea served chilled is a cold drink, here written in its common shortened form.

clue.text: Riddle — it may be black or white

definitions.meaning: to riddle is to perforate with holes, as with shot

definitions.text: it may be black or white
definitions.meaning: a ground spice from peppercorns comes in black and white forms

explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the verb meaning to shoot full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper a target is to riddle it with shot, and the seasoning from peppercorns is black or white.

clue.text: Low profile ultimately kept by him

indicators.note: being kept by someone means being held inside

parts.note: a chap is a man, a him

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A man keeps a low profile in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low profile' reads as one phrase but splits between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Low prices are inexpensive, and low behaviour is mean or shabby, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Spin bowlers possibly with a pinch of soil to pocket, hide

indicators.note: pocketing something means putting it inside, so one piece holds the other
spinning round turns the word back to front

parts.note: bowlers are hats, among others

indicators.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, here just the first letter

explanation.surface: Cricket spin bowlers rub a pinch of soil on the ball and pocket it out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin bowlers' suggests cricket, but bowlers are hats: HATS turned round is STAH, pocketing S.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to hide it away, typically in a secret store.

clue.text: See 8
Tick off an offence for one 15 24 33

indicators.note: off means not right, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: arson, setting fire to property, is a criminal offence

explanation.surface: A reprimand over a crime committed by a child playing at the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 24 33 reads 'playing at sixes and sevens': 6 and 7 down, cowboys and Indians. 'Tick off' reads as scold; 'off' rearranges TICK to KITC.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit Carson was a famous American frontiersman and scout, a cowboy in any game of cowboys and Indians.

clue.text: Endlessly drunk and endlessly sexy part of London

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

indicators.note: again the end of the word is dropped

parts.note: hot means sexy

explanation.surface: A district of London described as endlessly boozy and endlessly sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is London's West End district famed for nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a West End district of London known for its bars, clubs and theatres.

clue.text: See 24
Surrey town, say, served with 18

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means
18 across is red meat, and ham is a red meat

explanation.surface: A Surrey town where something is served with red meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham is a town in Surrey near Runnymede, the home of Royal Holloway college.
